content: Metoclopramide is prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, heartburn, stomach pain, bloating, and a persistent sensation of fullness after meals. It may also be used for other medical purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Metoclopramide is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Before taking metoclopramide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to metoclopramide or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially amobarbital (Amytal), insulin, narcotics (pain medications), phenobarbital, sedatives, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had an adrenal tumor, a seizure disorder, Parkinson's disease, high blood pressure, heart, liver, or kidney disease, a history of mental illness or depression, or an intestinal blockage or bleeding. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking metoclopramide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking metoclopramide. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Metoclopramide may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects, especially if they are severe or persistent: drowsiness, restlessness, fatigue, constipation, or diarrhea. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: involuntary movements of the limbs or eyes, spasms of the neck, face, or jaw muscles, or mood changes such as depression. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
